free_tier.stated: 1 TB hard limit per item page ("Currently, there is a 1TB size limit for item pages"), recommended 500 GB / 1,000 files per item; items per account unlimited. Single file "should not be larger than ~500 to ~700 GB".

egress.terms: Unmetered and free: every file in every item is a world-readable HTTP URL (https://archive.org/download/<id>/<file>) with no auth and no egress bill; IAS3 doc states "ACLs are fake. permissions are: World readable, Item uploader writable." Every public item additionally gets an _archive.torrent with IA webseeding as a second free distribution path.

tooling: IAS3 = S3-compatible REST (PUT = create item, multipart, x-archive-auto-make-bucket, x-archive-queue-derive:0, x-archive-size-hint); rclone backend 'internetarchive' (Tier 3, added v1.59, github.com/rclone/rclone 60.4k stars); official CLI/Python 'ia' github.com/jjjake/internetarchive (1,923 stars, pushed 2026-10-20); Rust client github.com/LucaCappelletti94/internetarchive-rs. S3 keys from archive.org/account/s3.php.
chaining: Unlimited items per account x 1 TB/item = unbounded per single free account. Also unlimited free accounts. 10 TiB hot set = 10-20 items of 500 GB-1 TB. 20 TiB archive = ~20-40 items. Zip many small files ("a zip file is considered one file" for the daily cap).
limits_note: 1 TB/item hard, 500 GB/item recommended; 500-700 GB single-file ceiling; 5,000 files/day across all items (zip counts as 1); recommended <=10,000 files/item but API accepts 250,000; DELETE bucket not allowed; S3 Range headers ignored; only HTTP/1.1 REST, no ACLs; every upload enters a per-item catalog queue plus a global derive queue that can block writes (503-slowdown-spam). Use x-archive-queue-derive:0 to skip expensive derivation.

reliability_note: Writes are asynchronous through a per-item queue; the global derive queue can stall uploads and deletes for hours during backlogs, and large/high-file-count items time out and fail to derive. Items are permanent (no TTL) but nothing is guaranteed private.
